correctness.rationale: Mixed independent sets are exactly the k missing pairs, giving the exact polynomial. On Re z >= 0, 2|1+z|^n >= 2+n|z|^2 > |kz^2-1| for 1<=k<=n, so the conclusion is strict. For z=-x, strict convexity on [0,1] and the signs at 0, 1/n and 1 give exactly two distinct roots there (the second is at the endpoint exactly when k=1); at n=3 even the largest k gives 2(2/3)^3+3/9=25/27<1. Above 1 the even case is positive; in the odd case (x-1)^(n-1)/x increases from zero to infinity, so the function rises and then falls to -infinity, with exactly one additional root. In the crown case the scalar sign limits at x=u/n and x=c/sqrt(n) bracket the ordered roots on separated scales; the outer odd root tends to 2 and satisfies n log(x-1)=log(2n)+o(1), giving the claimed expansion. Local uniform convergence of Z(u/n) to 2 exp(u)-1 and its simple zeros justify the fixed-mode lattice and identification of the real mode. The proof is exact; no sampled complex points or finite numeric tolerances are used to validate the universal assertions.
residual_risks: No extension asserted to nonmatching deletion, unequal shores, or uniform approximation in j; the supplied numeric tests would not establish such conclusions.

This is a usable classification for the family, not just an independence-polynomial tabulation or a phase-transition claim.
